system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Caveat:** The Seller's update calls these "key negotiated positions." Under playbook §0.4 and §6.3, that label doesn't make them agreed or cleared. The Seller's disclosure cut-off is 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026, so the underlying facts need refreshing before any position is conceded.

| ID | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation (one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** General liability cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m aggregate cap | 25% / AUD 6.0m | **Reject; counter at 25%/AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. |
| **SPA-N-002** De minimis & basket | De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; only the excess over the basket recoverable | De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded | **Reject.** The Seller's version is a deductible that would strip out most general claims. |
| **SPA-N-003** General claims time limit | 18 months after Completion; limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise | 24 months after Completion | **Reject; counter at 24 months.** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" wording also risks sweeping in Fundamental and Title claims. |
| **SPA-N-004** Fundamental/Title regime | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a basis for merging categories that the playbook keeps separate. |
| **SPA-N-005** Fraud carve-out | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; no fraud carve-out is stated | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable | **Reject; insert an express carve-out.** As drafted, the "any nature" wording would capture fraud, and no one may waive the carve-out. |
| **SPA-N-006** Disclosure scope | General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Letter 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7) | Specific fair disclosure only | **Reject.** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure is excluded by the playbook, and the playbook requires specific disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-007** Buyer knowledge qualifier | Buyer has no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (Clause 8.3) | Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and a reasonable-enquiry standard, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity | **Reject.** A blanket "discoverable" bar would turn the data room into a waiver of warranty claims. |
| **SPA-N-008** Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours only; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Letter 2: no final consent or evidence of conditions is included (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% revenue) | Effective consent AND evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion, not consent-on-delivery | **Reject.** Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent, and delivery does not establish that the consent is effective or its conditions are met. |
| **SPA-N-009** Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion. Letter 3: not repaid, no discharge | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | **Reject the post-completion release.** The playbook requires repayment and releases at Completion, and a deferred release would leave security over the business in place. |
| **SPA-N-010** Employee bonuses | DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. On-costs not addressed | AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item, or funded by the Seller | **Reject the silent exclusion.** The playbook requires a specific line item or Seller funding, and the on-costs remain unquantified. |
| **SPA-N-011** Ironquay IP indemnity | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000, unverified); described as "adequate" | Broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way | **Reject the narrow scope.** Limiting the indemnity to the SOW3 fee ignores the DD-004 transfer condition and any other exposure. |
| **SPA-N-012** Export/privacy incident (DD-006) | "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." Letter 6: not established as a breach, scope unknown, notification unresolved, no loss amount | No assumption of a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, require updates, and reserve rights | **Do not accept the materiality assertion.** The Seller's conclusion is unsupported, and the buyer should keep the investigation open with update obligations and reserved rights. |
| **SPA-N-013** Sandbar renewals | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000, described as ordinary-course operating costs (DD-008/DD-011) | Assess the renewals (terms, termination rights, whether committed or accrued). No automatic Debt classification or price deduction | **Assess, don't concede.** "Ordinary course" is an assertion, and the letter does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable or terminable. |
| **SPA-N-014** Category separation | Tax, IP and Title warranties all folded into the general regime; "same caps and time limits" for capacity/title | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate. No hidden general-regime override | **Reject.** Folding categories together is the mechanism that would override the Title and Tax regimes. |
| **SPA-N-015** Title verification | Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012 | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority (e.g., a current ASIC company extract, a PPSR search and the executed share transfers) | **Reject DD-012 as sole proof.** The register is a Seller-supplied internal source, not independent verification. |
| **SPA-N-016** Tax/IP open terms | Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" | Tax and IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution | **Reject "settled."** No agreement exists on these terms, and the general regime's caps should not be assumed to apply. |

**Other points to flag:**
- **Letter 1.4 (no admission):** The "not legally required" language should not be accepted as a characterisation of any consent, notice, payment or remediation. For example, the Mossvale restriction (Letter 9) and office-lease notice (Letter 7) need separate confirmation of whether consent is actually required.
- **Refresh required:** All disclosure facts date from 22 September 2026. Confirm the current position on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-005, DD-006 and the Sandbar renewals before relying on any of them.
- **Authority:** Amelia Frost's written approval is needed for the 20% cap and 18-month period, and none has been given. Until that is in place, the buyer's counter should stay at 25%/AUD 6.0m and 24 months.
=== END ADVICE ===
